title: Regional slot allocator and failback playbook for dedicated fleets
creator: Liam Ortega
description:
Summary: Define and implement a regional slot allocator plus an operational failback playbook to enforce throughput guarantees and data residency constraints for multi-zone dedicated fleets. The allocator ensures reserved throughput per region, supports constrained spillover, and drives autoscaling policies that preserve SLAs while minimizing cost and cross-region egress.

Problem: Customers on Dedicated expect both throughput guarantees (committed slots) and strict residency constraints. Current placement logic either over-provisions in each zone (high cost) or allows uncontrolled spillover (risking residency violations and unpredictable latency). We need a controller that: (1) reserves capacity at the regional level with zone slices, (2) enforces soft affinity and bounded spillover into compatible zones, and (3) coordinates autoscaling with graceful failover and runbook-driven manual intervention.

Goals:
- Guarantee committed throughput per customer/contract with measurable SLOs.
- Ensure data residency constraints are never violated (no cross-region execution for residency-locked requests).
- Provide bounded graceful degradation: when local capacity is exhausted, redirect to permitted fallbacks or shed traffic according to policy.
- Minimize cold-start latency and KV cache thrash when failing over or resharding.
- Expose observability and playbook steps for on-call and SREs.

Scope: Regional and multi-zone dedicated fleets only (not hosted shared endpoints). Encompasses placement policy, allocator service, autoscale policy hooks, routing updates, telemetry, and runbook playbook.

Proposed design (high level):
1) Regional Slot Allocator service: tracks committed slots per customer per region. Slots are expressed as ephemeral "capacity tokens" tied to specific node pools and quantized GPU units. Token states: reserved, allocated, prewarmed, spill-escrow.

2) Zone-sliced reservations: each region reserves a minimum slice per zone (min_zone_slots) and keeps a region-level overflow pool. Normal allocation prefers zone-slice, then region overflow, then spill-escrow in compatible neighboring zones as defined by residency policy.

3) Spill-escrow and policy enforcement: spill-escrow is a temporary, limited mechanism allowing controlled cross-zone execution when the customer contract allows for regional but not strict-zone residency. The allocator rejects any placement that would violate strict residency. Spill limits configurable per contract: max_spill_qps and max_spill_duration.

4) Autoscaling integration: autoscaler uses two inputs: allocator demand signal and health/latency signal. Autoscale policies include: target_utilization (e.g., 70%), min_reserved (equal to committed slots), cooldown, predictive headroom (based on commit history and scheduled events). Scale-up occurs proactively when predictive headroom projects >20% sustained demand; scale-down is conservative with long cooldown and graceful_shrink windows to avoid SLA blips and KV cache churn.

5) Warm pools and KV cache preservation: when failing over, the allocator will prefer nodes with warm KV caches (tracked via cache-age tags). Prewarm workflows spin up minimal prewarmed instances in adjacent zones on sustained pressure to reduce cold-start impact.

6) Routing & failback playbook: routing is updated atomically with an allocation transaction. Playbook defines steps for: automatic failover (fast path, controlled), partial degrade (shed low-priority customers), operator notification, manual runbook for rebalancing and forced failback once capacity stable, and post-incident reconciliation of slot accounting.

Trade-offs:
- Strict residency enforcement increases cost (need more reserved capacity per region).
- Aggressive spill can lower cost but risks violating soft residency and increases egress costs and latency.
- Predictive autoscale reduces latency but requires accurate demand forecasting and increases risk of overprovisioning.

Telemetry and acceptance criteria:
- Metrics: region_committed_slots_usage, spill_escrow_qps, percent_requests_served_in_residency_region, failover_latency_95, KV_cache_warm_rate, allocation_rejection_rate.
- SLOs: committed throughput availability >= 99.95% per billing period; residency_violation_rate = 0 for strict contracts; failover_latency_95 < 300ms for in-region failover, < 800ms for permitted spill.
- End-to-end test harness simulating regional outage and verifying allocation, failover, and runbook steps in staging.

Operational runbook links and artifacts:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/REGIONAL-SLOT-ALLOCATOR-2026
- Staging runbook: https://redwood.ops/Runbooks/RegionalSlotAllocatorPlaybook
- Datadog dashboard (staging): https://app.datadoghq.com/dashboard/rgk-regional-allocator
- PR (work in progress): https://github.com/redwood-inference/server/pull/4120

Implementation plan (phases):
A) Prototype allocator + policy engine, integrate with simulator and unit tests (2 sprints).
B) Autoscaler hooks and prewarm orchestration in staging (1 sprint).
C) Canary in a single non-critical customer region, collect telemetry, refine spill settings (1 sprint).
D) Gradual rollout and runbook training for SRE/solutions teams (2 sprints).

Acceptance criteria (must pass before promoted to canary):
- All allocator unit and integration tests pass.
- Simulated regional outage runbook test passes in staging with metrics within thresholds.
- Security review completed and KMS/Audit logging verified.
- Playbook documented and SRE runbook walkthrough completed.
comments: 2026-01-18: Kickoff synced with PM and SRE. Agreed to prototype allocator as separate control plane service rather than bolting into existing orchestrator to keep blast radius small.
2026-01-21: Design review notes from Maya (PM): emphasize clear billing signals for reserved vs spill usage. Action: add metric region_committed_slots_billed.
2026-01-25: Engineering notes: we chose tokenized slot model to simplify accounting and reduce race conditions during placement. Liam implemented initial token allocator in the simulator repo.
2026-01-28: Security review scheduled. Early flags: need audit trail for cross-zone placement decisions and proof that strict-residency requests never leave region. Assigned: Noor (security).

2026-01-30: PR opened: server#4120. Contains proto for SlotAllocator API and basic placement policy. Code review comments from Sandeep: add unit tests for spill_escrow expiry and KV cache tag matching.
2026-02-01: SRE feedback on runbook: prefer a manual 'evacuate-to-escrow' step before automated cross-zone spill for high-risk customers. Will add configuration per customer.
2026-02-02: Updated policy: default max_spill_duration = 15m, max_spill_qps = 10% of committed; can be tightened per contract. Planning canary in eu-west-1 for Feb cycle.
